breaking_news.headline: Does Europe regret its bet on U.S. defense?
breaking_news.summary: Europe bet big on American defense technology and they're now paying the price. Years-long backlogs are underway due to production delays and the U.S. own military needs.

breaking_news.headline: Is there an opening for Nvidia's competitors, now that Jensen Huang is out?
breaking_news.summary: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Dylan Patel of the AI and semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis about Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and whether it opens up the field for Nvidia's competitors.

breaking_news.headline: These economists say in-person work boosts creativity, but office mandates fall short
breaking_news.summary: A pair economists argue in a new book that people are more creative and productive when they work together in person. But it's not enough for employers to simply order workers back to the office.

breaking_news.headline: Commerce Department under pressure for delaying export controls on Nvidia chips
breaking_news.summary: The U.S. Commerce Department is under scrutiny for clearing Chinese companies to handle Nvidia chips, despite national security concerns from cabinet officials and U.S. intelligence agencies.

breaking_news.headline: New rule aims to close loophole on chip exports
breaking_news.summary: The Commerce Department released a new rule designed to make it harder for China to gain access to America's most powerful computer chips using third-country data centers.

breaking_news.headline: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
breaking_news.summary: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates.

breaking_news.headline: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow?
breaking_news.summary: In late October, Google had the worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks: has Google been caught in "the innovator's dilemma"?

breaking_news.headline: Huang says he'd be "honored" to return to Nvidia as he agrees to testify to Congress
breaking_news.summary: The former Nvidia CEO's comments come as some in Silicon Valley have tried to argue that Huang was pushed out of the company too quickly amid a swirl of national security scandals.

breaking_news.headline: Trump lands in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
breaking_news.summary: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".

breaking_news.headline: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
breaking_news.summary: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.

breaking_news.headline: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
breaking_news.summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.

breaking_news.headline: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
breaking_news.summary: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.

breaking_news.headline: Russian military plane crashes killing all 19 on board
breaking_news.summary: Russia's defence ministry says a technical malfunction was the likely cause of the crash in the Kemerovo region.

breaking_news.headline: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
breaking_news.summary: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.

breaking_news.headline: Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
breaking_news.summary: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.

breaking_news.headline: Government must act now or lose Royal Mail, former minister warns
breaking_news.summary: The former business secretary says "undercutting" by rivals will make Royal Mail "unviable".

breaking_news.headline: US government confirms investigation into tech firm Megaspeed
breaking_news.summary: The Singapore-based company is suspected of helping to ship high-end AI chips from tech giant Nvidia to China, violating US export rules.

breaking_news.headline: How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China
breaking_news.summary: The new rules restrict chip exports and also access to their computing power, which China relies on heavily.

breaking_news.headline: We couldn't afford a house alone, so we bought one with strangers
breaking_news.summary: People who can't afford to get on the housing ladder are buying homes with someone they don't know.

breaking_news.headline: Speed camera fault may have allowed drivers to escape fines
breaking_news.summary: The Home Office has revoked approval that allowed footage from speed cameras to be used in evidence.
